articles.title: Amazon Has a Decent Sale on PS5 Games in the Run Up to Black Friday
articles.summary: When it comes to finding big discounts on physical video games, Black Friday is the time to watch out for. This sale event usually doesn't start up until November, but Amazon's been sneaking in some offers before then for eager shoppers to check out.
body: Requiem's deal price is actually a return to the price we saw during Amazon's recent October Prime Day sale event, which marked a full $20 discount off its MSRP. In a similar position is Star Wars Zero Company, which is just pennies away from its Prime Day price at the retailer, saving you just over $10 compared to paying its full cost.

Final Fantasy VII Rebirth is another that caught our eye - initially as part of the Square Enix sale that popped up at Amazon recently - that's also returned to its lowest price point at Amazon. Right now it's available for just $20, which is a steal in comparison to its launch price of $70. And with Final Fantasy VII Revelation coming out next year, this is a perfect time to play it if you haven't yet.

Another standout game on sale right now is Pragmata, which is also back down to its lowest point at the retailer. It did dip to $39.99 during the most recent October Prime Day sale at Amazon, but that was exclusive to Prime members. For everyday shoppers, this is still a nice discount to jump on for one of our favorite games of the year so far.

articles.title: 3 Very Different Survival Games from indie.io Featured in Steam Next Fest
articles.summary: October is the perfect time to dive into a survival game, and there are three from publishing platform indie.io that are part of Steam Next Fest from now until October 26. And these three prove that “survival game” can mean very different things and have completely different gameplay.
body: One is a co-op horror-comedy set in a coal mine, one is an open-world sandbox after a zombie apocalypse, and one sees you stranded alone on a 24-island archipelago after your ship mysteriously crashes. You can play all three games right now, with two of them having free demos as part of Steam Next Fest and one already fully released with a huge new content update for spooky season.

Three generations ago, the sky froze. Now, your coal mining town is perpetually covered in snow. You might think that would be the end of the mine, but nope, the state kept it open and is forcing miners to continue delving into its depths. That might sound a bit dystopian, but it’s a premise that Coal Duty mines for humor as well as coal.

It’s a co-op extraction game for between 1–5 players, and you play as a group of miners who must navigate the many dangers of the mine to survive and get out with the materials you gathered. Each run is procedurally generally, so you’ll need to work together with your teammates to figure out how to progress.

articles.title: Battlefield 1’s Jack Lowden Is One Of The Finalists For New James Bond, Apparently
articles.summary: As rumored, it appears that actor Jack Lowden, who played Lawrence of Arabia in EA's Battlefield 1, is a finalist to play James Bond. According to Deadline, "final auditions" for the role will take place over the next week, and the process will include screen tests.
body: Many expect the casting process for James Bond to do finalized relatively soon, with an official announcement coming before the end of the year.
In May this year, Bond movie production company Amazon MGM Studios said the search for the next James Bond actor was underway and that the film studio would not comment on the casting process.
Lowden is Scottish, and he would become just the second Scottish person to play James Bond, following Sean Connery. The character James Bond from the Ian Fleming book series is also Scottish.

Fans have been waiting a long time for the next James Bond movie, as the latest entry, No Time To Die, was released in 2021. However, it was expected to release much sooner, but had three delays due in part to COVID.

articles.title: Mike Mignola Resurrects the Hellboy Universe for B.P.R.D.: Declassified
articles.summary: Even the end of the world can't keep the Hellboy franchise down. Creator Mike Mignola is once again revisiting his most iconic horror universe for a new miniseries called B.P.R.D.: Declassified.
body: B.P.R.D.: Declassified is cowritten by Mignola and Chris Roberson (iZombie), with art by Norton (Battlepug) and colors by Hellboy mainstay Dave Stewart. The first issue also features a variant cover by Gabriel Hardman (Green Lantern: Earth One).

"We’ve been teasing around the edges of a larger story involving an occult cold war in the pages of Hellboy and the B.P.R.D. and elsewhere for a while now, usually in the background of another supernatural investigation or monster hunt of some kind,” said Roberson in a press release. “B.P.R.D.: Declassified is a chance to pull the curtain back a bit and focus our full attention on what’s been going on in the shadows, and to see that the agents of the B.P.R.D. aren’t the only players on the board. The stakes are higher than Susan Xiang and company ever suspected."
B.P.R.D.: Declassified #1 will be released on February 17. You can preorder a copy at your local comic shop.
For more, see our breakdown of the ending to Avengers: Armageddon and check out a revealing new preview of Star Wars/Marvel: Hope Assembles #1.

articles.title: Mass Effect 5 Dev Says BioWare Saw What Larian and CD Projekt Had Done in the RPG Space and Was Taking the Franchise to ‘The Next Level’
articles.summary: A former Mass Effect 5 developer has said that BioWare had seen what RPG powerhouses Larian and CD Projekt were achieving with their games, and was responding by taking Mass Effect to “the next level.”
body: Yesterday, EA sent shockwaves through the industry with the announcement that the next Mass Effect game was canceled and its developer, BioWare, was shutting down. Around 50 people were reportedly working on the game before development ended.

Since yesterday’s dramatic news, a number of people who had worked on Mass Effect 5 talked in vague terms about the game it was shaping up to be. On X / Twitter, New York Times bestselling author Catherynne M. Valente responded to a user who said, “A game industry that cannot figure out how to make a sequel to the literal best game of all time is a game industry that is fundamentally broken,” with: “We did figure it out. We were working on a great game. Just saying.”

One person who was laid off from BioWare, cinematic supervisor Tony de Waal, took to LinkedIn to say Mass Effect 5 would have been “something special,” offering players “a level of autonomy and choice that no other game has been able to match.”

“We saw what Larian and CD Projekt were bringing to the table with their latest offerings, and started down a path to bring Mass Effect to the next level while remaining true to the Trilogy,” he continued.

articles.title: Katana Zero DLC Is Still Coming, And It’s Apparently Freakin’ Huge Now
articles.summary: It's been a minute since we've heard anything about Askiisoft's samurai platformer Katana Zero, but the developer has re-re-reconfirmed that, yes, the DLC is still on the way--and it's big. Like, so big Askiisoft is basically calling it a sequel.
body: In a Bluesky post on October 22, Justin Stander of Askiisoft announced that the Katana Zero DLC has grown even bigger than when we last heard-- which was in March 2021. It's apparently now "the size of a full sequel" and comes with a soundtrack of over 30 new songs. There's no release date or anything else outside of this confirmation, but at least it's still coming.

This is wonderful news for any fan of the 2019 side-scrolling samurai platformer, though a release date would be better. It's starting to feel like Team Cherry's Hollow Knight: Silksong, what with how often Askiisoft confirms the DLC is coming but doesn't say exactly when. After all, the last time we heard about the project was in April 2025, when Askiisoft said it's "still coming" and "still free." This is no shade, of course. I'd just like to play the DLC already.

articles.title: Why Street Fighter Movie Goes For “Gonzo” Vibes Instead of Gritty And Grounded
articles.summary: Street Fighter movie director Kitao Sakurai has shared new insights into the recently released video game movie, including how he intentionally wanted it to go for a "gonzo" style of over-the-top action and silliness as opposed to being gritty and grounded.
body: "There’s a silliness to it, and there’s an absurdity to the world and the characters and how they interact. [Producer] Cale Boyter at Legendary really held the torch for this vision of Street Fighter that had a gonzo energy to it. I also love comedy and craziness and energy," he told The Hollywood Reporter.

Also in the interview, Sakurai discussed how his work on The Eric Andre Show informed his filmmaking sensibilities for Street Fighter. He said he learned from that show that not every minute needs to be hilarious, but "every minute needs to be interesting."

"So there can be elements that are so ridiculous they might not track narratively or make sense conceptually, but because they’re part of an overall energy and feeling, they fit. So I kept that in mind when I was developing this film," he said.

Also in the interview, Sakurai talked about how Street Fighter's original movie directors, the Philippou brothers, ended up appearing in cameo roles. He said he personally invited them to appear in the movie as two people... fighting in the street.

articles.title: Resident Evil Director Zach Cregger Feels “Gratified” Following Gamer Backlash To His Highly Successful Movie
articles.summary: Resident Evil director Zach Cregger has responded to the success of his video game movie, and while he doesn't want to say “I told you so” to his haters, he's happy with the response, both critically and commercially. “I don’t know if I feel vindicated,” he told A Shot. “I’m gratified.
body: The Resident Evil movie has earned $363 million globally, making it the highest-grossing Resident Evil movie of all time and the highest-rated. It's also the No. 9 highest-grossing video game movie ever.

Prior to Resident Evil's release, Cregger said he was "naive" to think gamers would embrace his vision for the movie. People wanted to see a direct adaptation of one of the Resident Evil stories, featuring familiar plotlines and characters, but Cregger's movie didn't do any of that.

In the new interview, Cregger said the "problem with the internet" is that it's generally anonymous and people who dig their heels in and never apologize or change their mind. So instead, Cregger said he's no longer going to interact with those people and just make the stuff he wants.
“The only real way, I feel like, to do anything with it is to just not engage with it and just move on with your life," he said.

articles.title: Magic: The Gathering Turns 2 of the Best Star Trek Episodes Into Sagas
articles.summary: Magic: The Gathering ’s Star Trek Universes Beyond set is drawing inspiration from across the sci-fi franchise’s 60 year history, including references to all of its shows and films.
body: "Sagas have emerged as an exceptional design tool for presenting story arcs from other universes because of their episodic nature," senior editor Matt Tabak told Polygon. "Each chapter of a Saga can focus on an individual story beat, so when you put them together, you get a great overview of an entire episode in only a few abilities."

All Good Things… is named after the TNG series finale. The machinations of the near omnipotent trickster Q cause Picard’s mind to jump between the show’s present day, the period just before the Enterprise's first mission in the series premiere, and 25 years in the future. In each timeline, the Enterprise encounters a temporal anomaly that could prevent life from evolving on Earth. Picard must synchronize all three versions of his ship to protect the timeline and prove to Q that humanity is worth preserving.

articles.title: Universes Beyond Is About to Ruin the best Magic: The Gathering Set of the Year
articles.summary: Being a Magic: The Gathering fan has become an intense hobby. While the beauty of Magic lies in its variety, as the game offers ample choice of formats and ways to play, the quick pace of new set releases has affected the Magic experience overall.
body: Reality Fracture is by far one of the best Magic sets to come out in 2026. It brought a long-running storyline to a close (even if it wasn’t very satisfying ), culminating in the death of Jace Beleren, one of the game’s most iconic characters. Moreover, in terms of the Limited format, Reality Fracture is surely the best set of the year. Limited play (Draft or Sealed) is one of the most common ways to experience a new Magic set, as you play only with cards from that set. Limited players have been singing the praises of Reality Fracture since its debut, but unfortunately that's ending soon, making way for a new Universes Beyond set: Star Trek.

Reality Fracture was released on Oct. 2, with prerelease events starting on Sept. 25. It's the sixth of seven Magic sets released in 2026 (eight if you count Mystery Booster Commander Edition ). Reality Fracture succeeds in translating flavor and story into interesting gameplay mechanics. The most notable element is the presence of the Jace planeswalker tokens created through the Empower Jace mechanic. These are available to all colors and have a big impact on the set's Limited gameplay, but that's not all that Reality Fracture has going on.

articles.title: Final Fantasy 14, Umamusume: Pretty Derby, and more impacted as PHP vulnerability outages hit games around the globe
articles.summary: Multiple games - including Final Fantasy 14 and Umamusume: Pretty Derby - have faced outages and other issues following this week's discovery of a serious PHP vulnerability.
body: This vulnerability could potentially result in substantial security breaches for the massive number of websites and applications built using the PHP programming language. As a result, it was advised that online services built upon it should be taken offline until a fix could be distributed and applied. Inevitably, games were caught up.

An official post made to the Final Fantasy 14 lodestone website informed users that security "enhancements" were being made to the MMO's patch servers. As a result, new logins were temporarily disabled until the updates could be completed. While logins have since been turned back on, the server back-up feature for user's save data remains offline.

Horse racing gacha game Umamusume: Pretty Derby, meanwhile, was taken offline completely. As its server-side infrastructure uses PHP, a sudden maintenance outage was put in place - though its developer assured players no exploitation of the security vulnerability had occurred. Right now, Japanese and global servers are back online, with a compensatory package of in-game currency being sent to all players.
points: Multiple games - including Final Fantasy 14 and Umamusume: Pretty Derby - have faced outages and other issues following this week's discovery of a serious PHP vulnerability.

articles.summary: The hunt for the next James Bond is almost over. More than five years after Daniel Craig bowed out as Bond in Cary Joji Fukunaga's No Time to Die, another 007 is about to receive his license to kill.
body: Insiders told Deadline that four offers to participate in the tests have been sent out, with three of these going to Jack Lowden, Callum Turner, and Josh O’Connor. Six potential Bonds are reportedly on the shortlist to succeed Craig.

These tests were originally planned for earlier in the month, but the final auditions were pushed back due to scheduling conflicts. While the auditions are imminent, there’s no timeline for Amazon's final decision, though most expect it by the end of 2026; Amazon MGM producer Amy Pascal previously suggested as much.

The search for the next Bond heated up earlier this year when Amazon MGM brought on casting director Nina Gold. She was the inaugural winner of the Oscars’ Best Casting category for Hamnet, and previously cast Game of Thrones, Chernobyl, Conclave, and several Star Wars films.

articles.title: BioWare's cancelled Mass Effect game would've learned from Baldur's Gate 3 and The Witcher to deliver "a level of autonomy and choice that no other game has"
articles.summary: EA has closed its longtime studio partner BioWare, the iconic development house behind Mass Effect and Dragon Age, impacting around 50 staff who were in pre-production on the next Mass Effect game.
body: Tony de Waal, a BioWare veteran who has worked on previous Mass Effect and Dragon Age games, offered a rare look behind the scenes at what the team was attempting. In a LinkedIn post (via PC Gamer ), de Waal suggested the studio wanted to surpass the acclaimed work of the role-playing giants at Baldur's Gate 3 studio Larian and CD Projekt Red, maker of The Witcher and Cyberpunk.

"I was one of the lucky ones who stayed with BioWare to start on the next Mass Effect, where I believe we were making something special: a level of autonomy and choice that no other game has been able to match," de Waal wrote. "We saw what Larian and CD Projekt were bringing to the table with their latest offerings, and started down a path to bring Mass Effect to the next level while remaining true to the trilogy," he added.

The veteran cinematics lead sadly didn't offer any examples of what that could've looked like in-game, but given previous Mass Effect games have incorporated a great deal of player freedom, the idea of a sequel that builds on that - while incorporating modern techniques from CDPR and Larian - would certainly have been exciting.

articles.title: Despite its mixed reception, Marvel's Wolverine was September's top-selling new game in the US, making Sony launch revenues it hasn't seen since Helldivers 2
articles.summary: Marvel's Wolverine may not have had the best critical reception, but that clearly didn't discourage consumers. The action-adventure from Marvel's Spider-Man studio Insomniac has topped US video game sales in September, despite releasing exactly halfway through the month.
body: That's according to market analysis firm Circana, which noted Wolverine's success includes digital sales and those made at retail. It was such a hit that, as Circana analyst Mat Piscatella wrote, the game delivered "the highest launch month dollar sales" a Sony-published game has seen since Helldivers 2, which released in February 2024. It is worth noting, however, that Helldivers 2 launched on PC alongside PlayStation 5, while Wolverine is a PS5 exclusive. Additionally, Helldivers 2 had a much lower price of $40 compared to Wolverine's $70, meaning the former sold more copies to arrive at a similar point.

Wolverine seemingly helped boost PS5 sales, too, as the console saw a massive 43 percent uptick in dollar sales compared to the same period last year, though some of that is owed to its higher price now compared to then. In fact, PS5 led the month in both unit sales (up 22 percent from last year) and dollar sales across consoles. Switch 2 unit sales fell by 14 percent and Xbox by 27 percent - according to Circana, that means Xbox unit sales dropped to their lowest ever in a September, claiming the record from September 2025.
